title: Oncall Briefing Notes — 2026-06-30
content:
Purpose: quick handoff + weekly SRE sync notes (short form). Audience: oncall, SRE leads, infra eng.

Summary (top-line):
- This week saw three customer-impacting incidents (one brief P1, two P2s) and a recurring slow-start pattern on the generation-api under cold KV cache. Error budget consumption for generation-api rose to 28% (30-day window) after the P1; remaining budget for month-end is ~72%.
- Canary lane throttling experiments continue; early results show 12% improvement in tail latency for small requests when we route 20% of traffic to low-batch lanes. Plan: expand to 30% after A/B for 48h.
- Action priority: finalize KV cache warmup mitigations, stabilize routing fallback order, and clear postmortem queue (3 outstanding).

Incidents (concise timelines):
1) INC-2026-06-24 (P1) — generation-api spikes, downstream timeouts
   - Timeline: 06/24 09:05 UTC — 09:42 UTC
   - Symptom: sudden spike in 5xx (gateway 504s) for hosted model endpoints in us-west1; large fanout during a customer batch job overlapped with autoscaler flapping.
   - Root cause (current hypothesis): rapid burst of long-context requests exhausted ephemeral worker pool; autoscaler oscillation produced higher queuing and ELB timeouts. KV cache cold misses amplified token compute per request.
   - Mitigation executed: manual scale-up (+40% pool) and temporary throttling of bursty customer via rate-limiter rule (rl-rule-187) at 09:19 UTC.
   - Status: RCA in progress (assigned to @Liam, JIRA: JIRA-INF-1024). Probable fixes: smoother scale-up cooldown, add request-cost-based admission control, pre-warm KV caches for scheduled batch windows.
   - Customer comms: outbound by CS at 2026-06-24 14:00 UTC (internal copy linked in slack).

2) INC-2026-06-26 (P2) — routing fallback mis-order
   - Timeline: 06/26 04:40 UTC — 06/26 06:05 UTC
   - Symptom: 2xx but degraded latency for requests routed to quantized model variant in eu-west1; fallback routing unexpectedly preferred quantized variant due to outdated perf profile.
   - Mitigation: revert routing policy to baseline profile and drain affected hosts.
   - Action: product + serving-runtime to add automated profile verifier on rollout (task: JIRA-INF-1038). Owner: Marta.

3) INC-2026-06-28 (P2) — cache eviction storm
   - Timeline: 06/28 12:11 UTC — 06/28 13:00 UTC
   - Symptom: sudden drop in prefix cache hit-rate from 78% to 31% for a subset of tenant keys after batch maintenance job cleared shared shard indices.
   - Mitigation: temporarily bumped cache TTL and kicked warmup job for top-100 tenants. Monitoring alert added to detect >20% drop in 10m.
   - Follow-up: adjust shard maintenance script to be tenant-aware and add explicit warmup hook.

SLO snapshot (30-day rolling):
- generation-api availability (p99 success): target 99.95% — actual 99.72% (error budget used 28%).
- routing-latency (p95): target <120ms — actual 145ms (recent spike due to P2 on 06/26).
- kv-cache-hit-rate: target 70% — actual 61% (post-eviction dip). Threshold alert now set at 60%.

Oncall Handoff (what incoming oncall should know):
- Current pages assigned: 3 active (see linked JIRA). Two are in mitigation/monitoring; one (INC-1024) awaits RCA additions.
- Runbook notes:
  - generation-api slow-start: if KV cache hitrate <50% and request queue depth >200, trigger manual scale and enable implicit admission-control flag (runbook id: rb-gen-05).
  - Route fallback: if rollout profile mismatch suspected, flip to rollback-and-drain, do not edit policy via console if traffic >10k rps.
- Short-term experiment: canary-lane A/B (20% -> 30%). Watch p99 latency and cost per token metric; abort if p99 > baseline + 15%.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Finalize automatic KV warmup job that runs pre-scheduled batch windows (Devon) — ETA 2026-07-05.
- Add rollout profile verifier to rollout pipeline (Marta) — ETA 2026-07-03.
- Create admission-control prototype that considers request token-estimate (Liam) — spike due 2026-07-02.
- Clear postmortem backlog (priority: INC-1024, INC-1038, INC-1041) — owners assigned; aim to publish summaries by 2026-07-07.

Operational notes / misc observations:
- Observed noise in SLI ingestion between 02:00-03:00 UTC each morning (likely batch export job). Need to move heavy exports to off-peak or use sampled telemetry.
- Reminder: scheduled maintenance for cache-shard compaction on 2026-07-02 01:00 UTC — expect temporary hit-rate dip; notify CS and customers with high-throughput jobs.
- Cost note: small-model lanes are showing better unit cost but slightly worse p99 for >2k token requests; include this in next Optimize review.

Post-shift checklist (for off-going oncall):
- Ensure all active incidents have an owner and status field updated in JIRA.
- Leave explicit next-step for any mitigation in progress (don’t assume follow-up will be obvious).
- Confirm handoff message posted in slack:#oncall-handoffs with key metrics + links.

Open questions / things to discuss in weekly sync:
- Acceptance criteria for KV warmup feature: how to measure ROI? (cost vs latency reduction)
- Should we make rollout-profile verification blocking for canary traffic >10%?
- How to better surface long-tail token-cost estimations in routing decisions?

Notes to self (quick):
- Draft a short FAQ for CS about autoscaler backoff behavior — they got repeated tickets asking why scale-down appears to be "slow".
- Double-check runbook rb-gen-05 steps match actual tooling commands (recent CLI flags changed).

Attachments / links (quick list):
- JIRAs: JIRA-INF-1024 (P1 RCA), JIRA-INF-1038 (routing profile verifier), JIRA-INF-1041 (cache warmup task)
- GitHub PR: infra/pull/678 — admission-control prototype branch
- Confluence: serving-runtime/kernels + rollout-playbook

Signed-off-by: Aisha Kapoor — oncall lead (week of 2026-06-29)
